Hassan expects consumers to face another difficult period and the situation to remain unresolved until well into 2027.

You know, they're clearly concerned that that's going to spill over into non fuel prices. We feel that on balance that signals a follow on hike in November to ensure that inflation's tracking back to target. The question there's not so much about whether the economy is soft or weak, it's whether it's showing sufficient demand and weakness to ensure inflation comes back to target on a reasonable time frame. And at the moment that doesn't look likely with another supply shock rolling through things. And some of the strength outside of the consumer space is part of that picture too, particularly the data centre investment boom, which is supporting non consumer demand across the economy as well. headline: Forecasts July CPI headline at 3.3% year-ended, well below June's 3.8%, driven largely by base effects in electricity prices
reasoning: Neha Sharma expects a 0.8% monthly lift in July CPI but a significant drop in the year-ended rate to 3.3% from 3.8% in June. The main driver of the decline is base effects from strong electricity price rises last year not repeating. Upward pressures include auto fuel (excise discount rolling from 32c to 16c), seasonal holiday travel increases, and water and property rates. Electricity, via lower default market offers in most states, is expected to be the main offset.
quote: So in terms of the July CPI data that's coming out tomorrow, we're expecting a 0.8% lift in the month. That's quite a strong number at face value. But the year ended pace, we are actually expecting quite a significant drop to 3.3% from 3.8% in June. And a lot of this is due to base effects. So we saw electricity prices last year come up quite strongly, and we're not expecting the same level of impulse there.
